subject: geography
title: Country Spotlights: Kenya, Nigeria, Egypt
welcome_lead: Three African nations, three stories. Discover Kenya's wildlife, Nigeria's giant cities and Egypt's ancient riverlands.
meta_desc: KS3 Geography adventure on Kenya, Nigeria and Egypt as African case studies.
final_note: Brilliant! You can now describe three key African countries.

walkthroughs.body_html: Kenya is famous for its Maasai Mara and the Great Migration of wildebeest. Tourism is a major industry, with safaris attracting millions of visitors.
With over 200 million people, Nigeria is Africa's largest population. Lagos is one of the world's fastest growing megacities.
Egypt's people cluster along the Nile. Cairo is the capital. The pyramids of Giza are 4,500 years old!

mcqs.q: Why does plastic accumulate in ocean gyres?
options: Gyres are large rotating ocean currents driven by wind and Coriolis effect; floating debris is carried in but the rotation traps it in the centre, where currents are weak, concentrating plastic over decades.
The 'Great Pacific Garbage Patch' is a solid floating island of plastic you can walk on.
Plastic accumulates in gyres because the water there is denser.

Longshore drift carries sediment past a change in coastline direction (e.g. river mouth); deposition continues into deeper water, building a curved depositional landform with a hook.

mcqs.q: Why does oceanic crust subduct beneath continental crust?
options: A spit is a small island just off the coast.
Oceanic crust subducts because the ocean pushes it down with its weight.
Oceanic crust is denser (basaltic) than continental crust (granitic), so when they collide the denser oceanic plate sinks into the mantle, forming a trench and volcanic arc.
Continental crust subducts because it is thicker and heavier.
